properties.areaDesc: Seminole, FL
properties.description:
...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in Florida...

St Johns River Near Sanford affecting Seminole County.

.Heavy rainfall has caused river levels on the St. Johns near Sanford
to remain just below Minor flood stage. The river is forecast to
slowly climb into Minor flood stage later this week.

For the St. Johns River...including Sanford...Minor flooding is
forecast.

* WHAT...Minor flooding is forecast.

* WHERE...St Johns River near Sanford.

* WHEN...Until further notice.

* IMPACTS...At 5.5 feet, Water surrounds homes and covers some
driveways in the Stone Island area near Enterprise in Volusia
County. Water enters yards and floods docks in the River Oaks
Estates subdivision.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 7:30 PM EST Wednesday the stage was 5.4 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 4.2 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to rise to Minor Flood Stage
early Friday morning, where it will linger near 5.5 feet into
early next week. Additional rises are possible thereafter.
- Flood stage is 5.5 feet.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

properties.areaDesc: San Luis Obispo County Beaches; Santa Barbara County Central Coast Beaches
properties.description:
* WHAT...For the High Surf Advisory, large breaking waves of 10
to 15 feet with dangerous rip currents. For the High Surf
Warning, dangerously large breaking waves of 18 to 25 feet
with dangerous rip currents. For the Coastal Flood Warning,
significant coastal flooding expected.

* WHERE...San Luis Obispo County Beaches and Santa Barbara
County Central Coast Beaches.

* WHEN...For the High Surf Advisory, until 9 PM PST this
evening. For the High Surf Warning, from 9 PM this evening to
3 AM PST Sunday. For the Coastal Flood Warning, from 3 AM to 6
PM PST Saturday.

* IMPACTS...There is a high risk for flooding of sea water over
vulnerable low-lying coastal areas, especially around the time
of high tide. This includes significant flooding of coastal
beaches, walkways and roads, and potentially damaging some
structures. Significant beach erosion is expected. Powerful
waves and strong rip currents will pose an exceptional risk of
ocean drowning and damage to coastal structures like piers and
jetties. Large breaking waves can cause injury, wash people
off beaches and rocks, and capsize small boats near shore.
Remain far away from the water's edge.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...A series of west-northwesterly swells will
create an extended period of large surf into next week, with the
potential for WARNING level surf again late Sunday night through
Monday. Areas that may see most significant impacts will be
west-northwest facing beaches, with widespread flooding likely
at Oceano Dunes. Breaking waves may impact the Cayucos and Pismo
Beach piers as well as the Morro Bay Harbor entrance.
properties.headline: High Surf Warning issued November 13 at 8:12AM PST until November 15 at 3:00AM PST by NWS Los Angeles/Oxnard CA
properties.instruction:
Stay off of beaches and coastal walkways, roads, and structures.
Do NOT drive around barricades or through water of unknown depth.

Everyone should remain out of the water due to life-threatening
surf conditions. Stay off of jetties, piers, and other water side
infrastructure.

properties.description:
* WHAT...For the Beach Hazards Statement, dangerous rip currents

Advisory, large breaking waves of 4 to 7 feet Friday,
increasing to 7 to 12 feet Saturday. Surf heights are expected
to decrease to 6 to 9 feet Sunday through Tuesday.

* WHERE...Malibu Coast and Los Angeles County Beaches.

* WHEN...For the Beach Hazards Statement, until 2 PM PST this
afternoon. For the High Surf Advisory, from 2 PM this
afternoon to 3 PM PST Tuesday.

* IMPACTS...There is an increased risk of ocean drowning. Rip
currents can pull swimmers and surfers out to sea. Waves can
wash people off beaches and rocks, and capsize small boats
nearshore.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...A series of significant west-
northwesterly swells are expected to produce large surf into
next week with highest surf and greatest impacts likely
peaking Saturday and potentially again Monday. There is
potential for moderate coastal flooding impacts at times,
especially Saturday. Some of these impacts may be moderate to
significant beach erosion and shallow flooding of normal dry
beaches and walkways.

properties.areaDesc: San Luis Obispo County Beaches; Santa Barbara County Central Coast Beaches
properties.description:
* WHAT...For the High Surf Advisory, large breaking waves of 7 to
11 ft with dangerous rip currents through Friday. These waves
are expected to significantly increase Friday night into the
weekend, with waves between 18 to 25 feet possible on exposed
west to northwest facing beaches. For the Coastal Flood Watch,
significant coastal flooding possible.

* WHERE...San Luis Obispo County Beaches and Santa Barbara
County Central Coast Beaches.

* WHEN...For the High Surf Advisory, until noon PST Monday. For
the Coastal Flood Watch, from late Friday night through
Saturday afternoon.

* IMPACTS...There is a moderate risk of damaging flooding of sea
water over some vulnerable low-lying coastal areas, especially
around the morning high tide, including over beaches, roads, and
structures. Significant beach erosion is likely. There is an
increased risk for ocean drowning. Rip currents can pull
swimmers and surfers out to sea. Large breaking waves can cause
injury, wash people off beaches and rocks, and capsize small
boats near shore.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...A significant westerly swell is expected
this weekend with impacts likely peaking Saturday. Significant
beach erosion and WARNING-level surf is likely. Posing most
risk to west-northwest facing shores. Widespread flooding at
Oceano Dunes State Park is likely. Coastal hazards are likely
to continue well into next week.

near occupied lifeguard towers. Rock jetties can be deadly in
such conditions, stay off the rocks.

beaches and jetties from the high surf last weekend will pose
additional threats to those on the beaches and will exacerbate
coastal erosion.

of northerly winds, downstream tidal effects, and water from upstream
heavy rainfall working north through the basin.

forecast.

* WHAT...Moderate flooding is occurring and forecast.

* WHERE...St Johns River near Astor.possible

* WHEN...Until further notice.

Fish Camp and approaching sea wall at Blair's Jungle Den. Water
approaching sites closest to the river at Fish Tales RV Resort and
Astor Landing Campground. Portion of Clair Street covered by river
water south of the Butler Boat Ramp. Docks underwater at the Astor
Bridge Marina and along Riveredge Drive. Portions of Fox Road are
covered with water nearest to the river. Acorn, Hazelnut and Redbud
roads are underwater with yards inundated.

- Bankfull stage is 2.0 feet.

at 7:30 PM EST Friday was 2.7 feet.

in Minor Flood Stage through this weekend and into next week.
- Flood stage is 2.3 feet.

properties.instruction:
Slow down and use caution while traveling. The latest road conditions
for Illinois can be obtained at www.gettingaroundillinois.com. The
latest road conditions for Indiana can be obtained at
https://511in.org.

Be prepared for slippery roads. Slow down and use caution while
driving. If you are going outside, watch your first few steps taken
on stairs, sidewalks, and driveways. These surfaces could be icy and
slippery, increasing your risk of a fall and injury.

heavy snow to dry weather just a few miles away. Visibilities can
also vary greatly. Be prepared for rapid changes in weather,
visibility, and road conditions.

properties.areaDesc: San Luis Obispo County Beaches; Santa Barbara County Central Coast Beaches
properties.description:
* WHAT...For the High Surf Advisory, large breaking waves of 10
to 15 feet with dangerous rip currents. For the High Surf
Warning, dangerously large breaking waves of 18 to 25 feet
with dangerous rip currents. For the Coastal Flood Warning,
significant coastal flooding expected.

* WHERE...San Luis Obispo County Beaches and Santa Barbara
County Central Coast Beaches. Surf will we highest for west-
northwest facing beaches.

* WHEN...For the High Surf Advisory, until 9 PM PST Friday. For
the High Surf Warning, from 9 PM Friday to 3 AM PST Sunday.
For the Coastal Flood Warning, from 3 AM to 6 PM PST Saturday.

* IMPACTS...There is a high risk for flooding of sea water over
vulnerable low-lying coastal areas, especially around the time
of high tide. This includes significant flooding of coastal
beaches, walkways and roads, and potentially damaging some
structures. Significant beach erosion is expected. Powerful
waves and strong rip currents will pose an exceptional risk of
ocean drowning and damage to coastal structures like piers and
jetties. Large breaking waves can cause injury, wash people
off beaches and rocks, and capsize small boats near shore.
Remain far away from the water's edge.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...A series of west-northwesterly swells will
create an extended period of large surf into next week, with the
potential for WARNING level surf again late Sunday night through
Monday. Areas that may see most significant impacts will be
west-northwest facing beaches, with widespread flooding likely
at Oceano Dunes. Breaking waves may impact the Cayucos and Pismo
Beach piers as well as the Morro Bay Harbor entrance.
properties.headline: High Surf Warning issued November 12 at 6:38PM PST until November 15 at 3:00AM PST by NWS Los Angeles/Oxnard CA
properties.instruction:
Stay off of beaches and coastal walkways, roads, and structures.
Do NOT drive around barricades or through water of unknown depth.

Everyone should remain out of the water due to life-threatening
surf conditions. Stay off of jetties, piers, and other water side
infrastructure.

properties.areaDesc: South Washington Coast
properties.description:
* WHAT...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, tidal overflow flooding
expected. For the High Surf Advisory, large waves and hazardous
surf conditions. Breakers up to 30 to 35 feet.

* WHERE...South Washington Coast.

* WHEN...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, from noon today to 4 PM
PST this afternoon. For the High Surf Advisory, from noon
today to noon PST Saturday.

* IMPACTS...Minor flooding, up to one foot above ground level,
during high tides is expected in the low lying areas near bays,
sloughs, and the lower reaches of the coastal rivers.
Destructive waves may wash over beaches, jetties, and other
structures unexpectedly. People can be swept off rocks and
jetties and drown while observing high surf. Minor beach erosion
may damage coastal properties and buildings. Higher than normal
water run-up is expected on beaches and low-lying shoreline.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...The threat of sneaker waves is extreme
during these scenarios. Sneaker waves can suddenly knock people
off of their feet and quickly pull them into the frigid ocean
which may lead to serious injury or drowning. The sneaker wave
threat will peak this evening and tonight. In addition, the Toke
Point Tide gauge is forecast to reach approximately 11.2 ft
during high tide this afternoon.
properties.headline: Coastal Flood Advisory issued November 13 at 12:43AM PST until November 13 at 4:00PM PST by NWS Portland OR
properties.instruction:
A Coastal Flood Advisory means that tidal overflow flooding is
expected. Coastal residents in the warned area should be alert
for rising water, and take appropriate action to protect life and
property.

A High Surf Advisory means that high surf will affect beaches,
producing rip currents, sneaker waves and beach erosion. Stay
well back from the water's edge and be alert for exceptionally
high waves.

Keep away from large logs on the beach. Water running up on the
beach can easily lift or roll logs which can injure or kill
someone caught in their path.

properties.headline: Air Quality Alert issued November 11 at 11:29AM PST by NWS Los Angeles/Oxnard CA
properties.instruction:
To protect your health, check air quality levels and act as needed:

* When Air Quality Index (AQI) levels are "Unhealthy for
Sensitive Groups" (orange), sensitive groups as specified
above should limit extended or intense outdoor activity.
* When AQI is "Unhealthy" (red), everyone may experience health
impacts. Sensitive groups should avoid extended time outdoors.
* When AQI is "Very Unhealthy" (purple), sensitive groups should
avoid all outdoor physical activity. Everyone else should
avoid extended or intense outdoor activity.
* When AQI is "Hazardous" (maroon), everyone should avoid all
outdoor physical activity.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...

To help keep indoor air clean when air quality is poor:

* Keep windows and doors closed
* Run your air conditioner and/or an air purifier
* Do not use whole house fans or swamp coolers that bring in
outside air if you have other methods to stay cool
* Avoid other sources of pollution such as fireplaces, candles,
incense, grilling, and gasoline-powered lawn and garden
equipment

* WHAT...For the High Surf Warning, Dangerously large breaking
waves 30 to 35 feet. For the Coastal Flood Advisory, High
astronomical tides will cause minor flooding in low lying areas
around Humboldt Bay. 1.5 to 2.2 feet of saltwater inundation
above ground level is possible near shorelines and tidal
waterways. Between 8.7 and 8.9 feet MLLW at the North Spit tide
gauge is predicted.

* WHERE...Northern Coastal Humboldt County.

* WHEN...For the High Surf Warning, from 1 PM Friday to 4 AM PST
Sunday. For the Coastal Flood Advisory, from 11 AM to 3 PM PST
Friday. High tide is at 1:04pm at the Humboldt Bay North Spit
tide gauge. Saltwater inundation will be possible 1 to 2 hours
before and after high tide.

* IMPACTS...Flooding of low lying areas around Humboldt Bay
including parks and roads with only isolated closures
expected. Flooding will likely impact Jackson Ranch Road in
the Arcata Bottoms and several roads in King Salmon. Breaking
waves can sweep people off jetties and docks, and into
dangerous seas. Life- threatening surf conditions and
significant beach erosion can be expected.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...While astronomical tides are decreasing
each day, persistent southerly winds are aiding in raising water
levels for Humboldt Bay. The beginning of a very large incoming
swell could enhance coastal flooding if they overlap, but they
aren't anticipated to do so or will not overlap for long. After
only brief improvement in high swell late Saturday through
Sunday, a second large swell is forecast late Sunday through
Monday.

the U.S. Coast Guard for information regarding harbor and bar
closures.

possible.

abnormally high tides will result in Coastal Flooding.

time):
* Port Chicago: 1.2 ft above normal (6.1 ft MLLW) at 2:15 PM
Thu 11/12, 1.0 ft above normal (5.9 ft MLLW) at 2:56 PM Fri
11/13, 0.7 ft above normal (5.6 ft MLLW) at 3:44 PM Sat
11/14, and 0.3 ft above normal (5.2 ft MLLW) at 4:39 PM Sun
11/15.

PM Thu 11/12, 1.0 ft above normal (5.4 ft MLLW) at 6:10 PM
Fri 11/13, 0.9 ft above normal (5.2 ft MLLW) at 6:57 PM Sat
11/14, and 0.6 ft above normal (5.0 ft MLLW) at 7:50 PM Sun
11/15.
* Rio Vista (Datum NAVD88): +7.5 ft at 5:00 PM Thu 11/12,
+7.7 ft at 5:00 PM Fri 11/13, and +7.6 ft at 6:00 PM Sat
11/14.
- These predictions include up to +1.1 feet of storm surge that
will enhance the astronomical tide and flooding threat.
Timing of high tide may vary up to an hour throughout the San
Francisco Bay and Delta.

properties.areaDesc: South Washington Coast
properties.description:
* WHAT...For the High Surf Warning, large waves and dangerous surf
conditions. Breakers up to 30 to 35 feet. For the Coastal Flood
Advisory, tidal overflow flooding expected.

* WHERE...South Washington Coast.

* WHEN...For the High Surf Warning, until noon PST Saturday. For
the Coastal Flood Advisory, until 4 PM PST this afternoon.

* IMPACTS...Minor flooding, up to one foot above ground level,
during high tides is expected in the low lying areas near bays,
sloughs, and the lower reaches of the coastal rivers.
Destructive waves may wash over beaches, jetties, and other
structures unexpectedly. People can be swept off rocks and
jetties and drown while observing high surf. Severe beach
erosion may destroy coastal properties and buildings. Higher
than normal water run-up is expected on beaches and low-lying
shoreline.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...The threat of sneaker waves is extreme
during these scenarios. Sneaker waves can suddenly knock people
off of their feet and quickly pull them into the frigid ocean
which may lead to serious injury or drowning. The sneaker wave
threat will peak Friday evening into Friday night. In addition,
the Toke Point tidal gage is forecast to reach 11.2 feet during
high tide Friday afternoon, which is high enough to result in
tidal overflow flooding for a few hours around high tide.
properties.headline: High Surf Warning issued November 13 at 12:40PM PST until November 14 at 12:00PM PST by NWS Portland OR
properties.instruction:
A Coastal Flood Advisory means that tidal overflow flooding is
expected. Coastal residents in the warned area should be alert
for rising water, and take appropriate action to protect life and
property.

A High Surf Warning means that high surf will affect beaches,
producing rip currents, sneaker waves and beach erosion. Stay
well back from the water's edge and be alert for exceptionally
high waves.

Keep away from large logs on the beach. Water running up on the
beach can lift or roll logs which can injure or kill someone
caught in their path.

properties.description:
* WHAT...For the High Surf Advisory, large breaking waves of 5 to
8 feet today, increasing to 8 to 12 feet Saturday. Surf heights
are expected to decrease to 5 to 9 feet Sunday through Tuesday.
Dangerous rip currents expected. For the Coastal Flood
Advisory, minor to moderate coastal flooding expected.

* WHERE...Malibu Coast and Los Angeles County Beaches. Surf will
we highest for west-northwest facing beaches.

* WHEN...For the High Surf Advisory, until 3 PM PST Tuesday. For
the Coastal Flood Advisory, from 4 AM to 4 PM PST Saturday.

* IMPACTS...Moderate flooding of sea water is likely over some
vulnerable low-lying coastal areas that are normally dry,
especially around the time of high tide, including over beach
parking lots, bike paths, and harbor walkways. Moderate to
significant beach erosion is likely. Isolated damage is unlikely
but possible. There is an increased risk for ocean drowning.
Rip currents can pull swimmers and surfers out to sea. Large
breaking waves can cause injury, wash people off beaches and
rocks, and capsize small boats near shore.

vulnerable low-lying coastal areas, especially around the time

beaches, walkways and roads, and potentially damaging some
structures. Significant beach erosion is expected. Powerful
waves and strong rip currents will pose an exceptional risk of
ocean drowning and damage to coastal structures like piers and
jetties. Large breaking waves can cause injury, wash people
off beaches and rocks, and capsize small boats near shore.
Remain far away from the water's edge.

potential for WARNING level surf again late Sunday night through

west-northwest facing beaches, with widespread flooding likely
at low lying areas such as at Oceano Dunes. Breaking waves may
impact the Cayucos and Pismo Beach piers as well as the Morro
Bay Harbor entrance.

infrastructure.

properties.areaDesc: Los Angeles County Beaches; Los Angeles County Inland Coast including Downtown Los Angeles
properties.description:
* WHAT...The South Coast AQMD has issued an air quality alert due to
harmful levels of fine particle pollution.
Visit https://www.aqmd.gov/alertinfo to check current and forecasted
air quality levels.

* WHERE...in Maywood, Bell Gardens, Westmont, Hawthorne and
Manhattan Beach. Levels of particle pollution can vary by time and
location depending on emissions and local weather conditions.

* WHEN...until 11:59 PM Wednesday.

* IMPACTS...Particle pollution can get deep into the lungs and cause
serious health problems such as heart attacks, bronchitis, asthma
attacks, and difficulty breathing. Everyone can be affected, but
sensitive groups such as people with lung or heart disease, older
adults, people who are pregnant, children, and those who spend a lot
of time outdoors are at greater risk.
properties.headline: Air Quality Alert issued November 10 at 12:18PM PST by NWS Los Angeles/Oxnard CA
properties.instruction:
To protect your health, check air quality levels and act as needed:

* When Air Quality Index (AQI) levels are "Unhealthy for
Sensitive Groups" (orange), sensitive groups as specified
above should limit extended or intense outdoor activity.
* When AQI is "Unhealthy" (red), everyone may experience health
impacts. Sensitive groups should avoid extended time outdoors.
* When AQI is "Very Unhealthy" (purple), sensitive groups should
avoid all outdoor physical activity. Everyone else should
avoid extended or intense outdoor activity.
* When AQI is "Hazardous" (maroon), everyone should avoid all
outdoor physical activity.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...

To help keep indoor air clean when air quality is poor:

* Keep windows and doors closed
* Run your air conditioner and/or an air purifier
* Do not use whole house fans or swamp coolers that bring in
outside air if you have other methods to stay cool
* Avoid other sources of pollution such as fireplaces, candles,
incense, grilling, and gasoline-powered lawn and garden
equipment
properties.note: Non-Weather Emergency Message. Not sent to IPAWS.

St Johns River Near Astor affecting Volusia and Lake Counties.

.Heavy rainfall that has occurred upstream has resulted in continued
river levels in Minor Flood Stage. River levels are expected to
remain steady into the weekend as a large volume of water works north
through the basin, though developing northerly winds could generate a
small rise.

For the St. Johns River...including Astor...Moderate flooding is
forecast.

* WHAT...Moderate flooding is occurring and forecast.

* WHERE...St Johns River near Astor.

* WHEN...Until further notice.

* IMPACTS...At 2.8 feet, Docks and boat ramps covered at South Moon
Fish Camp and approaching sea wall at Blair's Jungle Den. Water
approaching sites closest to the river at Fish Tales RV Resort and
Astor Landing Campground. Portion of Clair Street covered by river
water south of the Butler Boat Ramp. Docks underwater at the Astor
Bridge Marina and along Riveredge Drive. Portions of Fox Road are
covered with water nearest to the river. Acorn, Hazelnut and Redbud
roads are underwater with yards inundated.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 7:30 PM EST Wednesday the stage was 2.7 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 2.0 feet.
- Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours ending
at 7:30 PM EST Wednesday was 2.8 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to remain steady above flood
stage at 2.7 to 2.8 feet.
- Flood stage is 2.3 feet.

properties.description:
* WHAT...For the High Surf Warning, dangerously large breaking
waves along the coast. For the Coastal Flood Advisory, minor
coastal flooding. Inundation of 1.75 to 2.25 feet above ground
level is possible along shorelines and low-lying coastal areas.

* WHERE...Grays Harbor County Coast zone.

* WHEN...For the High Surf Warning, until noon PST Saturday. For
the Coastal Flood Advisory, until 5 PM PST this afternoon.

* IMPACTS...Minor coastal flooding due to tidal overflow is
expected around high tide. This may lead to flooding of
parking lots, parks, and roads, with only isolated road
closures expected. Dangerous breaking waves can knock people
off their feet and sweep them into the ocean. Driftwood and
debris in powerful surf can injure or even kill people on the
beach observing the ocean. High surf will result in erosion to
beaches, dunes, and bluffs and may cause damage to roads,
trails, and coastal structures.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Significant log and debris pile-up on the
beaches and jetties from the high surf last weekend will pose
additional threats to those on the beaches and will exacerbate
coastal erosion.
properties.headline: High Surf Warning issued November 13 at 2:47PM PST until November 14 at 12:00PM PST by NWS Seattle WA
properties.instruction:
If travel is required, allow extra time as some roads may be
closed. Do not drive around barricades or through water of
unknown depth. Take the necessary actions to protect flood-prone
property.

Inundation above ground level refers to the height above the Mean
Higher High Water (MHHW) level.

Everyone should remain out of the water and well back from the
surf zone. This includes staying off jetties, piers, and other
coastal structures. Never turn your back on the ocean and keep
children and pets close. Know the tides and forecast conditions.
Follow warning signs and respect barriers.

properties.areaDesc: San Luis Obispo County Beaches; Santa Barbara County Central Coast Beaches
properties.description:
* WHAT...For the High Surf Advisory, large breaking waves of 10
to 15 feet with dangerous rip currents. For the High Surf
Warning, dangerously large breaking waves of 18 to 25 feet
with dangerous rip currents. For the Coastal Flood Warning,
moderate to significant coastal flooding expected.

* WHERE...San Luis Obispo County Beaches and Santa Barbara
County Central Coast Beaches. Surf will we highest
for west-northwest facing beaches.

* WHEN...For the High Surf Advisory, until 9 PM PST Friday. For
the High Surf Warning, from 9 PM Friday to 3 AM PST Sunday. For
the Coastal Flood Warning, from 3 AM to 6 PM PST Saturday.

* IMPACTS...There is a high risk for flooding of sea water over
vulnerable low-lying coastal areas, especially around the time
of high tide. This includes significant flooding of coastal
beaches, walkways and roads, and potentially damaging some
structures. Significant beach erosion is expected. Powerful
waves and strong rip currents will pose an exceptional risk of
ocean drowning and damage to coastal structures like piers and
jetties. Large breaking waves can cause injury, wash people
off beaches and rocks, and capsize small boats near shore.
Remain far away from the water's edge.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...A series of west-northwesterly swells
will create an extended period of large surf into next week,
with the potential for WARNING level surf again late Sunday
night through Monday. Areas that may see most significant
impacts will be west- northwest facing beaches, with
widespread flooding likely at low lying areas such as at
Oceano Dunes. Breaking waves may impact the Cayucos and Pismo
Beach piers as well as the Morro Bay Harbor entrance.

Advisory, minor to moderate coastal flooding expected.

* WHERE...Ventura County Beaches. Surf will we highest
for west-northwest facing beaches.

* WHEN...For the High Surf Advisory, until 3 PM PST Tuesday. For

* IMPACTS...Moderate flooding of sea water is likely over some
vulnerable low-lying coastal areas that are normally dry,
especially around the time of high tide, including over beach
parking lots, bike paths, and harbor walkways. Moderate beach
erosion is likely. Isolated damage is unlikely but possible.
There is an increased risk for ocean drowning. Rip currents
can pull swimmers and surfers out to sea. Large breaking waves
can cause injury, wash people off beaches and rocks, and
capsize small boats near shore.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...A series of significant west-
northwesterly swells are expected to produce large surf into
next week with highest surf and greatest impacts likely
peaking Saturday and potentially again Monday. Minor to
moderate coastal flooding impacts are possible, especially
when largest surf overlaps with peak high tides. Some of these
impacts may be moderate to significant beach erosion and
shallow flooding of normally dry beaches and walkways.

properties.areaDesc: Northern Coastal Humboldt
properties.description:
* WHAT...For the High Surf Warning, Dangerously large breaking
waves 30 to 40 feet. For the Coastal Flood Advisory, High
astronomical tides will cause minor flooding in low lying areas
around Humboldt Bay. One half foot of saltwater inundation
above ground level is possible near shorelines and tidal
waterways. Between 8.8 and 9.1 feet MLLW at the North Spit tide
gauge is predicted.

* WHERE...Northern Coastal Humboldt County.

* WHEN...For the High Surf Warning, from 1 PM Friday to 4 AM PST
Sunday. For the Coastal Flood Advisory, from 11 AM to 3 PM PST
Friday. High tide is at 1:04pm at the Humboldt Bay North Spit
tide gauge. Saltwater inundation will be possible 1 to 2 hours
before and after high tide.

* IMPACTS...Flooding of low lying areas around Humboldt Bay
including parks and roads with only isolated closures
expected. Flooding will likely impact Jackson Ranch Road in
the Arcata Bottoms and several roads in King Salmon. Breaking
waves can sweep people off jetties and docks, and into
dangerous seas. Life- threatening surf conditions and
significant beach erosion can be expected.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...While astronomical tides are decreasing
each day, persistent southerly winds are aiding in raising
water levels for Humboldt Bay. The beginning of a very large
incoming swell could enhance coastal flooding if they overlap,
but they aren't anticipated to do so or will not overlap for
long. After only brief improvement in high swell late Saturday
through Sunday, a second large swell is forecast late Sunday
through Monday.

high waves.

beach can easily lift or roll logs which can injure or kill
someone caught in their path.

properties.areaDesc: Northern Coastal Humboldt
properties.description:
* WHAT...For the High Surf Warning, Dangerously large breaking
waves 30 to 35 feet. For the Coastal Flood Advisory, High
astronomical tides will cause minor flooding in low lying areas
around Humboldt Bay. 1.5 to 2.2 feet of saltwater inundation
above ground level is possible near shorelines and tidal
waterways. Between 8.7 and 8.9 feet MLLW at the North Spit tide
gauge is predicted.

* WHERE...Northern Coastal Humboldt County.

* WHEN...For the High Surf Warning, from 1 PM Friday to 4 AM PST
Sunday. For the Coastal Flood Advisory, from 11 AM to 3 PM PST
Friday. High tide is at 1:04pm at the Humboldt Bay North Spit
tide gauge. Saltwater inundation will be possible 1 to 2 hours
before and after high tide.

* IMPACTS...Flooding of low lying areas around Humboldt Bay
including parks and roads with only isolated closures
expected. Flooding will likely impact Jackson Ranch Road in
the Arcata Bottoms and several roads in King Salmon. Breaking
waves can sweep people off jetties and docks, and into
dangerous seas. Life- threatening surf conditions and
significant beach erosion can be expected.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...While astronomical tides are decreasing
each day, persistent southerly winds are aiding in raising water
levels for Humboldt Bay. The beginning of a very large incoming
swell could enhance coastal flooding if they overlap, but they
aren't anticipated to do so or will not overlap for long. After
only brief improvement in high swell late Saturday through
Sunday, a second large swell is forecast late Sunday through
Monday.
properties.headline: High Surf Warning issued November 12 at 10:21PM PST until November 15 at 4:00AM PST by NWS Eureka CA
properties.instruction:
A Coastal Flood Advisory indicates that onshore winds and tides
will combine to generate flooding of low areas along the shore.

Feet Above Ground is locally defined as feet above the Highest
Astronomical Tide or HAT.

Large breaking waves along the coast will lead to increased wave
run-up on beaches with waves topping and washing over large rocks
and jetties. These large waves can be erratic and unpredictable.
Use extra caution near the surf zone as these large waves will be
capable of sweeping people into the frigid and turbulent ocean
water. Mariners traversing the bar are urged to exercise extreme
caution or stay in port until the threat subsides. Please contact
the U.S. Coast Guard for information regarding harbor and bar
closures.

properties.description:
* WHAT...Dangerously large breaking waves 30 to 40 feet.

* WHERE...Coastal Del Norte and Northern Coastal Humboldt
Counties.

* WHEN...Until 4 AM PST Sunday. .

* IMPACTS...Breaking waves can sweep people off jetties and
docks, and into dangerous seas. Life-threatening surf
conditions and significant beach erosion can be expected.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...After only brief improvement late
Saturday through Sunday, a second large swell is forecast late
Sunday through Monday.
properties.headline: High Surf Warning issued November 13 at 9:19PM PST until November 15 at 4:00AM PST by NWS Eureka CA
properties.instruction:
Large breaking waves along the coast will lead to increased wave
run-up on beaches with waves topping and washing over large rocks
and jetties. These large waves can be erratic and unpredictable.
Use extra caution near the surf zone as these large waves will be
capable of sweeping people into the frigid and turbulent ocean
water. Mariners traversing the bar are urged to exercise extreme
caution or stay in port until the threat subsides. Please contact
the U.S. Coast Guard for information regarding harbor and bar
closures.

mph.

* WHERE...In California, Lassen-Eastern Plumas-Eastern Sierra
Counties. In Nevada, Greater Reno-Carson City-Minden Area.

* WHEN...From 10 AM to 10 PM PST Friday.

* IMPACTS...Gusty winds will blow around unsecured objects. Tree

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Winds may knock down burned trees in the Davis

properties.headline: Wind Advisory issued November 11 at 11:52AM PST until November 13 at 10:00PM PST by NWS Reno NV
properties.instruction:
Now is the time to secure loose outdoor items such as patio
furniture, holiday decorations, and trash cans before winds increase
which could blow these items away. The best thing to do is prepare
ahead of time by making sure you have extra food and water on hand,
flashlights with spare batteries and/or candles in the event of a
power outage.

water in urban or other areas is occurring or is imminent.

area. Overflowing poor drainage areas have already caused minor
flooding in the advisory area.

flooding lingers across urban areas. Expect nuisance flooding to
trend downwards over the next two hours.

Berkeley, Richmond, Daly City, San Mateo, San Leandro, Redwood
City, Mountain View, Alameda and Union City.

properties.areaDesc: San Francisco; Southern Monterey Bay and Big Sur Coast
properties.description:
* WHAT...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, up to 1.5 ft of
inundation above ground level is possible in low-lying areas
near shorelines and tidal waterways. For the Beach Hazards
Statement, an increased risk for sneaker waves and strong rip
currents with breaking waves of 15 to 20 ft expected. For the
High Surf Warning, dangerously large breaking waves of 25 to
30 ft expected.

* WHERE...San Francisco and Southern Monterey Bay and Big Sur
Coast Counties.

* WHEN...For the Beach Hazards Statement, through Friday
afternoon. For the Coastal Flood Advisory, until 4 PM PST
Friday. For the High Surf Warning, from 6 PM Friday to 4 AM
PST Sunday.

* IMPACTS...High tides will result in flooding of low-lying
infrastructure, isolated road closures, and coastal erosion.
Rising tides will bring water and waves farther up the beach
than normal, restricting escape from beaches and coastal
areas. Dangerously large breaking waves can overpower
swimmers, pulling people into the sea from beaches, jetties,
and rocks resulting in significant physical injury and
increasing the risk of drowning. Waves can sweep across the
shoreline without warning, pulling people into the sea from
beaches, jetties, and rocks.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...At the San Francisco tide gauge, high tide
is expected to be: 1.3 ft above normal (7.1 ft MLLW) at 12:10
PM Thursday 11/12, 1.5 ft above normal (7.3 ft MLLW) at 12:49 PM
Friday 11/13. These predictions include up to 1.5 ft of surge
that will enhance the astronomical tide and flooding threat.
High tide varies up to 90 minutes earlier or later along the
Pacific Coast and through the San Francisco Bay, respectively.

15 feet with dangerous rip currents. For the High Surf Warning,
dangerously large breaking waves of 18 to 25 feet with dangerous
rip currents. For the Coastal Flood Warning, significant coastal
flooding expected.

* WHERE...San Luis Obispo County Beaches and Santa Barbara
County Central Coast Beaches. Surf will we highest for west-
northwest facing beaches.

* WHEN...For the High Surf Advisory, until 9 PM PST Friday. For
the High Surf Warning, from 9 PM Friday to 3 AM PST Sunday.
For the Coastal Flood Warning, from 3 AM to 6 PM PST Saturday.

* IMPACTS...There is a high risk for flooding of sea water over
vulnerable low-lying coastal areas, especially around the time
of high tide. This includes significant flooding of coastal
beaches, walkways and roads, and potentially damaging some
structures. Significant beach erosion is expected. Powerful
waves and strong rip currents will pose an exceptional risk of
ocean drowning and damage to coastal structures like piers and
jetties. Large breaking waves can cause injury, wash people off
beaches and rocks, and capsize small boats near shore. Remain
far away from the water's edge.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...A series of west-northwesterly swells will
create an extended period of large surf into next week, with the
potential for WARNING level surf again late Sunday night through
Monday. Areas that may see most significant impacts will be
west-northwest facing beaches, with widespread flooding likely
at Oceano Dunes. Breaking waves may impact the Cayucos and Pismo
Beach piers as well as the Morro Bay Harbor entrance.

properties.description:
* WHAT...For the Beach Hazards Statement, dangerous rip currents
and breaking waves due to elevated surf. For the High Surf
Advisory, large breaking waves of 4 to 7 feet this afternoon
through evening, increasing to 8 to 14 feet Friday through
Tuesday. Peak surf heights expected Saturday, possibly peaking
again Monday.

* WHERE...Ventura County Beaches. Surf will we highest for west-
northwest facing beaches.

* WHEN...For the Beach Hazards Statement, until 2 PM PST this
afternoon. For the High Surf Advisory, from 2 PM this
afternoon to 3 PM PST Tuesday.

* IMPACTS...There is an increased risk of ocean drowning. Rip
currents can pull swimmers and surfers out to sea. Waves can
wash people off beaches and rocks, and capsize small boats
nearshore.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...A series of significant west-
northwesterly swells are expected to produce large surf into
next week with highest surf and greatest impacts likely peaking
Saturday and potentially again Monday. There is potential for
moderate coastal flooding impacts at times, especially Saturday.
Some of these impacts may be significant beach erosion and
shallow flooding of normal dry beaches and walkways. Breaking
waves are possible at the Ventura Harbor entrance during peak
surf. There is a low chance for warning level surf Saturday.

properties.areaDesc: Mason, WA
properties.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall is possible.

* WHERE...A portion of northwest Washington, including the following
county, Mason.

* WHEN...From late tonight through late Saturday night.

* IMPACTS...Excessive runoff may result in flooding of rivers,
creeks, streams, and other low-lying and flood-prone locations.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- Three to four and a half inches of rain is forecast for the south
slopes of the Olympics between early Friday and early Sunday with
snow levels of 5500 to 6500 feet. The combination of heavy rain
and relatively high snow levels could push the Skokomish River
near Potlatch above flood stage.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

properties.description:
...The Flood Warning is extended for the following rivers in
Washington...

Skokomish River At Potlatch affecting Mason County.

* WHAT...Minor flooding is occurring and minor flooding is forecast.

* WHERE...Skokomish River at Potlatch.

* WHEN...Until early Thursday morning.

* IMPACTS...At 16.5 feet, the Skokomish River will cause widespread
flooding of pasture lands, with water flowing quickly over West
Bourgault Road and Skokomish Valley Road.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 6:30 PM PST Wednesday the stage was 16.6 feet.
- Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours ending
at 6:30 PM PST Wednesday was 17.6 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected subside below flood stage early
Thursday morning. The river will begin rising again Friday rising
above flood stage Friday afternoon and continue rising to a crest
of 17.4 feet late Saturday morning.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

St Johns River Near Cocoa 9w affecting Brevard County.

.Recent rainfall over the headwaters of the St. Johns River has
caused Major flooding at the gauge west of Cocoa. The river is
forecast to continue to rise within Major flood stage through this
weekend.

For the St. Johns River...including Cocoa 9w...Major flooding is
forecast.

* WHAT...Major flooding is occurring and major flooding is forecast.

* WHERE...St Johns River near Cocoa 9w.

* WHEN...Until further notice.

* IMPACTS...At 17.2 feet, Water enters homes along the St Johns River
in the Lake Poinsett area west of Cocoa, also low lying homes in
the Silver Pines subdivision in Rockledge and the Shakespeare Park
area of Cocoa. Providence Road area west of Cocoa becomes
impassable, cutting off access to homes in the Mullet Lane and Bass
Road area. Docks flooded and water in parking lot at Lone Cabbage
Fish Camp.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 7:15 AM EST Thursday the stage was 17.1 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 15.8 feet.
- Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours ending
at 7:15 AM EST Thursday was 17.1 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to slowly rise to 17.2 feet this
weekend.
- Flood stage is 16.0 feet.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

properties.areaDesc: Brevard, FL
properties.description:
...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in Florida...

St Johns River Near Cocoa 9w affecting Brevard County.

.Recent extreme rainfall over the headwaters of the St. Johns River
has caused the river near Cocoa to rise to Major Flood Stage. The
river is forecast to continue a gradual rise within Major flood stage
through this weekend.

For the St. Johns River...including Cocoa 9w...Major flooding is
forecast.

* WHAT...Major flooding is occurring and forecast.

* WHERE...St Johns River near Cocoa 9w.

* WHEN...Until further notice.

* IMPACTS...At 17.2 feet, Water enters homes along the St Johns River
in the Lake Poinsett area west of Cocoa, also low lying homes in
the Silver Pines subdivision in Rockledge and the Shakespeare Park
area of Cocoa. Providence Road area west of Cocoa becomes
impassable, cutting off access to homes in the Mullet Lane and Bass
Road area. Docks flooded and water in parking lot at Lone Cabbage
Fish Camp.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 8:15 PM EST Thursday the stage was 17.1 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 15.8 feet.
- Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours ending
at 8:15 PM EST Thursday was 17.1 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to slowly rise to 17.2 feet this
weekend.
- Flood stage is 16.0 feet.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

properties.areaDesc: Central Siskiyou County
properties.description:
* WHAT...For the Wind Advisory, south winds 20 to 35 mph with gusts
up to 55 mph expected. For the High Wind Warning, south winds 25 to
40 mph with gusts up to 70 mph expected.

* WHERE...Most of the Shasta Valley in central Siskiyou County. This
includes portions of Interstate 5 as well as the communities of
Weed, Gazelle, Grenada and Montague.

* WHEN...For the Wind Advisory, until 10 PM PST this evening. For the
High Wind Warning, from 10 PM this evening to 1 PM PST Friday.

* IMPACTS...Damaging winds will blow down trees and power lines.
Widespread power outages are expected. Travel will be difficult,
especially for high profile vehicles. Gusty winds will blow around
unsecured objects. Tree limbs could be blown down and a few power
outages may result.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Highways running west to east will be exposed
to tough driving conditions given the strong southerly wind speeds.
properties.headline: High Wind Warning issued November 12 at 1:17PM PST until November 13 at 1:00PM PST by NWS Medford OR
properties.instruction:

or damaged by the wind.

Winds this strong can make driving difficult, especially for high
profile vehicles. Use extra caution.

nws:urn:oid:2.49.0.1.840.0.f15fec456e5cf.title: Coastal Flood Warning issued November 12 at 6:52PM PST until November 13 at 12:00PM PST by NWS Seattle WA

properties.areaDesc: Grays Harbor County Coast
properties.description:
* WHAT...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, minor coastal flooding
expected. Inundation of 1.75 to 2.25 feet above ground level
is possible along shorelines and low-lying coastal areas. For
the High Surf Advisory, large breaking waves along the coast.

* WHERE...Grays Harbor County Coast zone.

* WHEN...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, from 11 AM to 5 PM PST
Friday. For the High Surf Advisory, from noon Friday to 7 AM
PST Saturday.

* IMPACTS...Minor coastal flooding due to tidal overflow is
expected around high tide. This may lead to flooding of
parking lots, parks, and roads, with only isolated road
closures expected. Large breaking waves can knock people off
their feet, move driftwood and debris, and crash over rocks
and jetties. People can be injured or drown while observing
the ocean. Localized beach and coastal erosion is expected.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Significant log and debris pile-up on the
beaches and jetties from the high surf last weekend will pose
additional threats to those on the beaches and will exacerbate
coastal erosion.
properties.headline: Coastal Flood Advisory issued November 12 at 6:52PM PST until November 13 at 5:00PM PST by NWS Seattle WA
properties.instruction:
If travel is required, allow extra time as some roads may be
closed. Do not drive around barricades or through water of
unknown depth. Take the necessary actions to protect flood-prone
property.

Inundation above ground level refers to the height above the Mean
Higher High Water (MHHW) level.

Never turn your back on the ocean and keep children and pets
close. Know the tides and forecast conditions. Follow warning
signs and respect barriers.

NWSheadline: HIGH SURF ADVISORY REMAINS IN EFFECT FROM NOON FRIDAY TO 7 AM PST SATURDAY

nws:urn:oid:2.49.0.1.840.0.f15fec456e5cf.title: High Surf Advisory issued November 12 at 6:52PM PST until November 14 at 7:00AM PST by NWS Seattle WA

properties.areaDesc: San Francisco; Southern Monterey Bay and Big Sur Coast
properties.description:
* WHAT...For the first Coastal Flood Advisory, Up to 1.5 ft of
inundation above ground level is possible in low-lying areas
near shorelines and tidal waterways. For the Beach Hazards
Statement, An increased risk for sneaker waves and strong rip
currents with breaking waves of 15 to 20 ft expected. For the
High Surf Warning, Dangerously large breaking waves of 25 to 35
ft, with occasional sets of 40 to 50 ft at favored breakpoints.
For the second Coastal Flood Advisory, large breaking waves will
run up beaches and crash over seawalls, inundating adjacent,
low-lying infrastructure.

* WHERE...San Francisco and Southern Monterey Bay and Big Sur
Coast.

* WHEN...For the first Coastal Flood Advisory, until 4 PM PST
Friday. For the Beach Hazards Statement, through Friday
afternoon. For the High Surf Warning, from 6 PM Friday to 4 AM
PST Sunday. For the second Coastal Flood Advisory, from
midnight Friday night to 6 PM PST Saturday.

* IMPACTS...High tides will result in flooding of low-lying
infrastructure, isolated road closures, and coastal erosion.
Rising tides will bring water and waves farther up the beach
than normal, restricting escape from beaches and coastal
areas. Dangerously large breaking waves can overpower
swimmers, pulling people into the sea from beaches, jetties,
and rocks resulting in significant physical injury and
increasing the risk of drowning. Waves can sweep across the
shoreline without warning, pulling people into the sea from
beaches, jetties, and rocks.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...At the San Francisco tide gauge, high tide
is expected to be: 1.3 ft above normal (7.1 ft MLLW) at 12:10 PM
Thursday 11/12, 1.5 ft above normal (7.3 ft MLLW) at 12:49 PM
Friday 11/13. These predictions include up to 1.8 ft of surge
that will enhance the astronomical tide and flooding threat.
High tide varies up to 90 minutes earlier or later along the
Pacific Coast and through the San Francisco Bay, respectively.
The Coastal Flood Advisory on Saturday is specifically for the
Pacific Coast, where large breaking waves will spill over sea
walls and run up beaches onto adjacent infrastructure.

properties.areaDesc: Southwestern Lake; Eastern Lake
properties.description:
* WHAT...South winds 20 to 25 mph with gusts up to 45 mph expected.

* WHERE...Southeastern Lake.

* WHEN...From 7 AM to 2 PM PST Friday.

* IMPACTS...Wind gusts will be particularly strong along windward
ridges and exposed coastal headlands.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Winds will be strong aloft and may mix down to
the surface, resulting in wind advisory conditions.
properties.headline: Wind Advisory issued November 12 at 2:34PM PST until November 13 at 2:00PM PST by NWS Eureka CA
properties.instruction:
Winds this strong can make driving difficult, especially for high
profile vehicles. Use extra caution.

NWSheadline: WIND ADVISORY REMAINS IN EFFECT FROM 7 AM TO 2 PM PST FRIDAY

nws:urn:oid:2.49.0.1.840.0.fce54782b8c07.title: Wind Advisory issued November 12 at 2:34PM PST until November 13 at 2:00PM PST by NWS Eureka CA

properties.areaDesc: Greater Lake Tahoe Area; Greater Lake Tahoe Area
properties.description:
* CHANGES...Increased wind gusts.

* WHAT...Heavy wet snow. Snow accumulations near 12 inches above 7000
feet, with up to 6 inches below 7000 feet. Snow accumulations up to
20 inches along the crest west of Lake Tahoe. Wind gusts of 70 to
90 mph over ridges and gusts of 45 to 55 mph for Truckee and Lake
Tahoe communities. Wave heights 2 to 5 feet on Lake Tahoe.

* WHERE...Greater Lake Tahoe Area.

* WHEN...From 10 AM Friday to 10 AM PST Saturday.

* IMPACTS...Travel could be very difficult. The hazardous conditions
could impact the Friday evening commute. Strong winds and Sierra
cement snow could cause damage to trees and power lines. Strong
winds and rough waves on Lake Tahoe will create hazardous
conditions for small watercraft.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...A burst of heavy snow is likely with this
system late Friday afternoon into Friday evening with snow levels
falling to as low as 5500 feet.
properties.headline: Winter Storm Warning issued November 12 at 12:34PM PST until November 14 at 10:00AM PST by NWS Reno NV
properties.instruction:

vehicle in case of an emergency. The latest road conditions for the
state you are calling from can be obtained by calling 5 1 1.

properties.description:

areas along US-395/I-580 may see gusts up to 65 mph.

* WHERE...In California, Lassen-Eastern Plumas-Eastern Sierra
Counties. In Nevada, Greater Reno-Carson City-Minden Area.

* WHEN...From 10 AM to 10 PM PST Friday.

* IMPACTS...Gusty winds will blow around unsecured objects. Tree
limbs could be blown down and a few power outages may result.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Winds may knock down burned trees in the Davis
Fire burn area.
properties.headline: Wind Advisory issued November 11 at 1:04AM PST until November 13 at 10:00PM PST by NWS Reno NV
properties.instruction:
Now is the time to secure loose outdoor items such as patio furniture
and trash cans before winds increase which could blow these items
away. The best thing to do is prepare ahead of time by making sure
you have extra food and water on hand, flashlights with spare
batteries and/or candles in the event of a power outage.
